Define an event source

Source: R/lang_v2.R
omop_event.Rd

An event is a typed row source over one OMOP table: the rows of the table (restricted to a concept set when one is given), narrowed by a row predicate (where) and an optional visit restriction, with the numeric value normalised by unit before any predicate or reducer reads it.

Usage

omop_event(
  table,
  concepts = NULL,
  descendants = FALSE,
  mapped = FALSE,
  exclude = NULL,
  where = NULL,
  visit = NULL,
  value = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  concept_col = NULL,
  end = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  on_missing_table = c("error", "unavailable")
)

Arguments

table

OMOP table with a role record (any event table; not cost, provider, location, care_site or episode_event, which are reached through the bounded adapters omop_cost and omop_episode_members).

concepts

Concept IDs, an omop_concept_set, the name of a registry concept set, or NULL for every row of the table.

descendants, mapped, exclude

Expansion flags used when concepts is a vector of IDs (see omop_concept_set).

where

NULL or a row predicate from omop_where / omop_where_tree over the table's filterable columns and the normalised value.

visit

NULL, list(type = <visit_concept_ids>) or "index" (the visit of the index event).

value

Name of the numeric value column (default: the table's value role, value_as_number where present).

unit

NULL or an omop_unit conversion.

concept_col

Scope the concepts on another concept column (for example "unit_concept_id").

end

NULL (the table's end column), "start" (point events) or list(fallback = "days_supply").

name

Event name (registry key; generated when NULL).

on_missing_table

"error" (default) or "unavailable": a site without the table gets a typed unavailable state (criteria UNKNOWN, numeric and count features NA) instead of a failure.

Value

An omop_event object.

See also

omop_where, omop_unit, omop_era, omop_variable

Examples

hba1c <- omop_event("measurement", 3004410,
  unit = omop_unit(8554, convert = list("8753" = c(factor = 0.0915, offset = 2.15))),
  where = omop_where(!is.na(value)), name = "hba1c")
